newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul prosecutors seek warrant for Hanbo chairman.
newsitem.headline: Seoul prosecutors seek warrant for Hanbo chairman.

text.p: South Korea's state prosecutors on Friday sought an arrest warrant for the chairman of the troubled Hanbo Group whose steelmaking flagship collapsed in January, a prosecution official said.
"We have filed an application for the warrant to arrest Mr Chung Bo-keun on charges of embezzlement," he said.
The official accused Chung of pocketing about 37 billion won ($41 million) from Hanbo Group funds. Hanbo, with 22 member firms, is South Korea's 14th largest industrial conglomerate.
Chung's father, Hanbo founder Chung Tae-soo, is standing trial along with nine other people in connection with a loans-for-kickbacks scandal that has rocked the nation.
Prosecutors reopened their probe into the Hanbo scandal after the opposition attacked an earlier investigation as a whitewash which failed to bring to justice major players.
Prosecutors have said they would seize assets of the Chung family to "end the bad practice of the past when businessmen survived even when their businesses collapsed".
